category: PCB Layout (ARES): footprint libraries, pre-production checks, 3D & manufacturing output
description: Turning a routed Proteus board into a manufacturable, documented release: package and style libraries, the connectivity and design rule checks (including the silkscreen rules), the 3D Visualizer with STEP/IGES/STL exchange, and the CADCAM, ODB++, pick-and-place, BOM, graphics and batch Output Job Manager deliverables.

tools.name: Package Mode and the package library
tools.description: Places PCB packages (footprints) directly on the layout, independent of the schematic — used for mounting holes, fiducials, tooling features and mechanical items. The package library is browsed by keyword and category in the same way as the device library, with a preview of the pads and outline.
tools.usage: Package Mode on the left toolbar > P to browse the package libraries > pick and place
tools.example: Package Mode > P > keyword 'MOUNTINGHOLE' > place four at the board corners.

tools.name: Make Package
tools.description: Turns pads, 2D graphics and a reference origin drawn on the layout into a reusable library footprint. The dialog asks for the package name, category, sub-category and type (through-hole or surface mount) and the library to save into, and the result becomes available to Make Device's packaging step.
tools.usage: Select the pads and graphics > Library > Make Package…

parameters.name: Category / Sub-category / Type
parameters.description: Classification used by the package browser's filters.

parameters.name: Package Library
parameters.description: User library the footprint is written into.

tools.example: Place the pads on a 0.5 mm grid, draw the silkscreen outline and the pin-1 marker, select all, Library > Make Package > name 'QFN32_5X5' > save to USERPKG.
tools.notes: Include an origin marker and the silkscreen outline before making the package; adding them later means re-making it.

tools.name: Pad styles, trace styles and via styles
tools.description: Proteus draws all copper through named styles rather than per-object dimensions: pad styles (round, square, DIL, SMT, polygonal, with drill and mask settings), trace styles (named widths such as T10, T15, T40) and via styles (pad and drill diameters). Editing a style changes every object that uses it, which is how a board-wide width or annular ring change is made in one step.
tools.usage: Technology > Edit Pad Styles… / Edit Trace Styles… / Edit Via Styles…

parameters.name: Pad style
parameters.description: Shape, size per layer, drill hole, solder mask and paste settings, and whether the pad is plated.

parameters.name: Trace style
parameters.description: Named track width applied by net class or chosen manually.

parameters.name: Via style
parameters.description: Via pad diameter and drill size, plus the legal drill span.

tools.example: Technology > Edit Trace Styles > add style 'T40' at 1.0 mm and assign it to the POWER net class; every power track picks it up.

tools.name: Connectivity Rule Check (CRC)
tools.description: Verifies that the copper on the board matches the netlist from the schematic: it reports unrouted connections, tracks that connect nets which should be separate, and copper that is not connected to anything. Together with the DRC it is the pre-production gate — a board with CRC errors is wired differently from its schematic.
tools.usage: Tools > Connectivity Rule Check (Tools > Design Rule Check reports the geometric errors)
tools.example: Tools > Connectivity Rule Check > review the report; double-click an entry to select the offending copper.

tools.name: Design Rule Check (DRC) and silkscreen DRC
tools.description: Checks the layout's geometry against the design rules: clearances between copper objects, to the board edge and to graphics, plus the silkscreen checks added in recent releases — silk-to-silk (overlapping legends that would smear together) and silk-to-solder-mask (ink printed over an exposed pad or mask opening, a common fabrication rejection).
tools.usage: Tools > Design Rule Check; silkscreen rules are configured in Technology > Design Rule Manager
tools.example: Enable the silk-to-solder-mask rule, run the DRC, and move the designators that overlap pad openings.
tools.notes: Run the DRC again after adding teardrops, zones or copper thieving — all three add copper that can consume clearance.

tools.name: 3D Visualizer
tools.description: Renders the board and its components in 3D from the layout and the attached 3D models, with rotation, cross-sectioning and view presets. It is used to check component heights, connector positions and enclosure fit, and it updates live as the layout changes because it reads the same project database.
tools.usage: 3D Visualizer tab in the application shell (or Output > 3D Visualization)
tools.example: Switch to the 3D Visualizer, rotate to a side view, and confirm the electrolytic clears the enclosure lid.

tools.name: 3D model import and export (STEP / IGES / STL)
tools.description: Brings mechanical models in and sends the assembled board out. Component 3D models are attached in STEP or IGES form so the visualizer shows real bodies, and the whole board — outline, copper and components — is exported as STEP, IGES or STL for the mechanical CAD package or for 3D printing an enclosure mock-up.
tools.usage: 3D Visualizer > Output > Export 3D Model (STEP / IGES / STL); attach component models through the package's 3D properties
tools.example: Export the populated board as STEP and hand it to mechanical for the enclosure model; import the enclosure's IGES to check clearance in Proteus.

tools.name: CADCAM output (Gerber and Excellon)
tools.description: The main manufacturing output: Gerber X2 (the primary supported format, carrying layer function and netlist attributes) or traditional RS-274X, together with Excellon drill files and the drill tool table. The dialog chooses which layers are plotted, the units and format, whether files are combined or separate, and whether an IPC-D-356 netlist is included.
tools.usage: Output > Generate CADCAM Files…; select layers, format and destination

parameters.name: Layers
parameters.description: Which copper, mask, paste, silk, drill and mechanical layers are output.

parameters.name: Format
parameters.description: Gerber X2 or RS-274X, units and coordinate resolution.

parameters.name: Drill output
parameters.description: Excellon drill files, with plated and non-plated separated.

parameters.name: IPC-D-356 netlist
parameters.description: Electrical test netlist shipped alongside the artwork.

tools.example: Output > Generate CADCAM Files > Gerber X2, metric, all used layers, separate plated/non-plated drills, include IPC-D-356 > Generate.
tools.notes: Regenerate the zones and re-run the DRC and CRC before generating CADCAM output, and view the result in the Gerber viewer before sending it.

tools.name: Gerber viewer / CADCAM preview
tools.description: Loads the generated Gerber and drill files back into Proteus so the artwork can be inspected layer by layer exactly as the fabricator will see it. Checking the output rather than the design is what catches missing zones, wrong layer selections and silkscreen over pads.
tools.usage: Output > Gerber View… (load the generated file set)
tools.example: Output > Gerber View > select the generated folder > step through each layer and confirm the ground plane and the drill file are present.

tools.name: ODB++ output
tools.description: Writes the intelligent, single-package ODB++ data set — copper, masks, paste, drills, stackup, netlist and component data together — which removes the layer-mapping ambiguity of a Gerber folder and is preferred by most assembly houses that support it.
tools.example: Output > Export ODB++ > archive the result and send one file to the fabricator instead of a Gerber folder plus a layer list.

tools.name: Pick and Place file
tools.description: Exports the component centroid data the assembly machine needs: reference, value, package, X and Y position, rotation and board side, per assembly variant so not-fitted parts are excluded. The units and origin are selectable and must match what the assembler expects.
tools.usage: Output > Pick and Place File…; choose the format, units and origin
tools.example: Output > Pick and Place File > CSV, metric, origin at the board's bottom-left datum > pickplace.csv.

tools.name: Bill of Materials (from the layout)
tools.description: Generates the parts list for assembly, including the PCB package for each line and honouring the current assembly variant and the per-part 'exclude from BOM' flags. Output formats are HTML, PDF, CSV and Excel, with configurable columns.
tools.usage: Output > Bill of Materials > HTML / PDF / CSV / Excel
tools.example: Output > Bill of Materials > Excel, variant 'WiFi' — the not-fitted parts are omitted from the list.

tools.name: Output Job Manager
tools.description: Batch manufacturing output: a saved job lists every output a release needs — Gerber X2, Excellon, ODB++, pick and place, BOM, PDF drawings, 3D exports — with its settings and destination, and generates them all in one operation. It makes a release repeatable rather than a remembered sequence of individual commands.
tools.usage: Output > Output Job Manager…; define the job's outputs and destination folder, then run it
tools.example: Create a 'Release' job containing Gerber X2, drills, ODB++, pick and place and the BOM, and run it after every DRC-clean revision.
tools.notes: Introduced with Proteus 9.2; earlier releases generate each output from its own Output-menu command.

tools.name: Print and export graphics (PDF, DXF, bitmap)
tools.description: Documentation output from the layout: printing selected layers at a chosen scale, and exporting the artwork as PDF, DXF, bitmap, metafile or EPS. The DXF export is what a mechanical engineer usually wants for the board profile and mounting-hole positions.
tools.usage: Output > Print…, Output > Export Graphics > (PDF / DXF / Bitmap / Metafile / EPS); Output > Set Output Area to restrict the region
tools.example: Output > Export Graphics > Export DXF > Board Edge and drill layers only > outline.dxf for the mechanical team.

tools.name: DXF and Eagle import
tools.description: Brings foreign data into the layout: DXF for board outlines, enclosure geometry and mechanical keep-outs, imported onto a chosen layer with a selectable scale and unit; and Eagle design import for migrating boards from that tool. Getting the DXF units right on import is essential or the outline arrives at the wrong scale.
tools.usage: File > Import > DXF… (choose the target layer, units and scale); File > Import for the supported foreign design formats
tools.example: File > Import > DXF > enclosure.dxf > units mm, scale 1:1, target layer Board Edge > Import.

tools.name: Board dimensions and measurement
tools.description: Measures distances on the layout and places dimension annotations on a documentation layer, for the fabrication drawing and for confirming mechanical requirements such as connector positions and mounting-hole spacing.
tools.usage: The measurement/dimension tools in the PCB Layout module, placed on a documentation or silk layer
tools.example: Dimension the board width and the mounting-hole pitch onto the mechanical layer before exporting the fabrication drawing.
